question: At the pair class largest executed key [1,512,512,128] on BLACKHOLE, does a change of STORAGE WIDTH convert to time? Every prior bfp8 realization number in this campaign is Wormhole (b2z-bfp8-narrow, 0.26-0.30 at c_z=128) and the one Blackhole byte number (c14-byte-deletion, 1.9% of the op for 50% of its DRAM bytes) is a DESTINATION RETARGET, not a width cut, so it does not answer this.

rate_provenance.clone_same_shape_where: c14-byte-deletion, qb1 node 0 (p150a, 110 cores), 1350 MHz, ttnn.clone on this exact key = 82.4% of the roof
rate_provenance.class_where: c10-fold-census on qb2 at a during-sampled 1350 MHz

reasoning.clone_f32: the opposite-direction control demanded by memory dtype-narrowing-byte-discount-needs-opposite-direction-control: if doubling the bytes does not roughly double the time, narrowing cannot halve it and the whole axis is dead on this class.
reasoning.clone_b8: 0.531x the bytes but block float is not a byte-for-byte move: the packer re-derives one shared exponent per 16-element block. ttnn.permute on bfloat8_b already measures 1.13-1.44x SLOWER than bf16 on 0.53x the bytes (ttx-reblock-bfp8-pairtrack), so a pure mover is expected to keep well under half the byte cut.
reasoning.ln_b8: layer_norm is at 96.5% of a same-shape clone at this key (c14-byte-deletion) so it is byte-bound here, but removing gamma/beta made it 1.43x SLOWER, i.e. the affine term is load-bearing work a width cut cannot touch.
reasoning.mul_b8: multiply_ and add_ read 415.9 and 423.6 GB/s in-fold against a 442.9 roof, 94-96%, the least non-byte slack in the fold.
reasoning.linear_b8act: c13-matmul-rate fitted the thin-K key as t(kt) = 0.0723 + 0.00554*kt ms, 73.9% of the time at K=128 not scaling with K at all, measured with DRAM traffic removed. A width cut cannot touch a per-output-tile pipeline cost.

what_would_make_it_negative: clone_f32 < 1.40x -> the class is not byte-bound at this key and bfp8 has no mechanism here; the row closes with that as the answer.
clone_b8 >= 0.95x -> the block format own pack/unpack cost eats the byte cut on a pure mover, so no downstream region can pay however it is scoped.
any arm throwing on a bfp8 operand -> that op is not bfp8-capable and the region containing it needs a conversion at that edge, which is charged against the region.
aa_floor_rule: the bf16 clone arm runs twice per rep as its own A/A twin; a session whose A/A floor exceeds 1.0% is discarded, not reported.
